references.text: God promises Abraham that he will make his descendants into a great nation—the same promise now given to Jacob as he is about to go down to Egypt.
God tells Isaac not to go down to Egypt—a contrast to the message Jacob now receives, telling him not to fear going there.
God reveals himself to Isaac and says "Do not be afraid," promising to bless him—the same kind of revelation and encouragement that Jacob receives.
God reveals himself to Jacob at Bethel and promises that his descendants will become numerous—a promise now reaffirmed at Beersheba.
God confirms the promise to Jacob that a nation and an assembly of peoples will come from him—a promise pointing toward Israel's growth in Egypt.
Jacob recalls that God Almighty revealed himself to him in Luz and promised to make him into an assembly of peoples.
The children of Israel were fruitful, multiplied greatly, and became very powerful in Egypt—the direct fulfillment of God's promise to make Jacob a great nation there.
Moses reminds us that Jacob went down to Egypt with few people and became a great, mighty, and numerous people—a summary of the fulfillment of God's promise.
Theological contrast: The promise of protection in Egypt versus the warning against becoming defiled there.
